answer: A newcomer receives one kernel of standing, planted in a shared meadow where strangers can watch it grow. The kernel sprouts only through public, stranger-checked work: each job waters it, each verified delivery adds a leaf, and a lantern of past deeds hangs above it for anyone to inspect. A farm fails because one operator cannot water fifty kernels in different soils at once, so its meadow stays bare and identical while honest kernels branch apart. Privileges grow only as the plant grows, and a withered kernel must be replanted alone under new strangers.
